summary: Find the longest substring in which every character occurs at most twice.
mainInsight: The same window as 'at most k occurrences' with k = 2: after adding s[r], shrink from the left while its count exceeds 2.

approaches.name: Sliding window with counts
approaches.summary: Count characters in the window and shrink when one exceeds 2.

promptVariants: Which technique solves this in O(n)?
What kind of window problem is this?
options: Variable sliding window with counts (at most 2 occurrences)
Binary search on the substring length with a check
Dynamic programming over prefixes with two states
A trie holding every substring seen so far
cards.answer: Variable sliding window with counts (at most 2 occurrences)
cards.explanation: Validity is local to the newly added character.

promptVariants: Why do you only need to fix the count of s[r]?
How is this problem related to the 'at most k frequency' subarray problem?
cards.answer: The window was valid before adding s[r], so only s[r] can have exceeded 2 occurrences. It is exactly the 'at most k frequency' problem with k = 2 on characters.
keyPoints: Only the new character can violate

cards.explanation: Each index enters and leaves the window once.

promptVariants: Space complexity with a bounded alphabet: ___
Complete the statement: Space complexity with a bounded alphabet: ___
cards.explanation: The count map has at most one key per distinct character (alphabet size).

promptVariants: Why does the while loop condition check `cnt[s[r]] > 2` and not the left character?
What does the left pointer remove while shrinking?
cards.answer: The violation is caused by the character just added, so the loop continues until one of its earlier copies has been removed - which happens when l passes the first of its three copies. Characters removed on the way are decremented accordingly.
keyPoints: Shrink until the earliest copy leaves
cards.explanation: Same loop as the k-frequency version.

promptVariants: How long can the window be?
cards.explanation: Any window of 'a' contains more than two copies once its length exceeds 2.

incorrectOptionExplanations.4: The entire string has four copies.
